content.title: Costco hit with another class action lawsuit
content.text: NewsCostco gas. Kirkland. Gas station in New Jersey on Friday, March 20, 2026. Patti Sapone | NJ.com Costco’s been hit with a class-action lawsuit related to how it handled renewals.Plaintiff Russel George’s suit alleges Costco sends its customers an email notice 60 days prior to charging their credit cards for membership renewals, TopClassAction reports. violatesThat timeframe is outside the 45-day window set by California’s Automatic Renewal Law. The law, which went into effect in July 2025, is designed to make it easier to cancel subscription and sets requirements for notifications.“Due to Costco’s untimely and deficient auto-renewal notice, the plaintiff was deprived of information he was statutorily entitled to that would have notified him of the upcoming auto-renewal and provided him with methods of cancellation,” the Costco class action lawsuit said.Had he been notified of the charge in “a timely manner,” the suit said, “he would have canceled his membership and not gone forward with the auto-renewal.”The suit also claims Costco violated California’s False Advertising Law, Consumer Legal Remedies Act and Unfair Competition Law. George is seeking a jury trial along with damages for himself and other class members.Costco charges $65 for a basic Gold Star membership and $130 for an Executive membership. Members can cancel memberships by calling a toll-free number or visiting a warehouse store.A preliminary hearing in the case is scheduled for June.Earlier this year, the warehouse club was hit with a lawsuit related to its chicken processing plant in Nebraska. The suit alleged the plant is contaminated with Salmonella and failed safety standards set by the U.S. Department of Agriculture.Leada Gore has worked with AL.com for 13 years.
